problems.title: 3Sum
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a list of integers, return every distinct three-value combination whose sum is zero. Combination and result ordering are unrestricted.

## Example

Input `[-1, 0, 1, 2, -1, -4]` returns the combinations `[-1, -1, 2]` and `[-1, 0, 1]`.

problems.title: Alien Dictionary
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given words already sorted according to an unknown alphabet, return an ordering that contains every distinct input character exactly once and is consistent with the word order. Return an empty string if no such ordering exists; if several orderings are valid, any one is accepted.

## Example

Input `["wrt", "wrf", "er", "ett", "rftt"]` returns `"wertf"`.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given prices in time order, return the greatest profit from at most one transaction: buy once and sell once later. Making no transaction is allowed, so return zero when every buy-before-sell pair has no positive profit.

## Example

Input `[7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 4]` returns `5`.

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a binary-tree root, return node values grouped by depth from the root, with each level ordered from left to right.

## Example

The tree `[3, 9, 20, null, null, 15, 7]` returns `[[3], [9, 20], [15, 7]]`.

problems.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a nonempty binary tree, return the largest sum along a connected path of nodes. The path may start and end at any nodes.

## Example

The tree `[-10, 9, 20, null, null, 15, 7]` returns `42`.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a stair count, return the number of ways to reach the top when each move climbs one or two stairs.

## Example

Input `5` returns `8`.

problems.title: Clone Graph
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a node in a connected undirected graph, return a structurally equivalent deep copy. No node in the result may reuse an input node.

## Example

A four-node cycle with adjacency `[[2,4], [1,3], [2,4], [1,3]]` returns an independent graph with the same adjacency.

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given coin denominations and a target amount, return the fewest coins that total the amount, or `-1` when no combination does.

## Example

Coins `[1, 2, 5]` and amount `11` return `3`.

problems.title: Combination Sum
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a finite list of positive candidate integers and a target, return all combinations that sum to the target. A candidate may be selected repeatedly; the values within each combination and the combinations in the result may appear in any valid order.

## Example

Candidates `[2, 3, 6, 7]` and target `7` return `[2, 2, 3]` and `[7]`.

problems.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given preorder and inorder value traversals of one binary tree whose node values are distinct, reconstruct and return its root.

## Example

Preorder `[3, 9, 20, 15, 7]` and inorder `[9, 3, 15, 20, 7]` produce tree `[3, 9, 20, null, null, 15, 7]`.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given vertical-line heights in index order, return the maximum area held between two lines and the baseline.

## Example

Input `[1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7]` returns `49`.

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a list of integers, return whether any value occurs more than once.

## Example

Input `[1, 2, 3, 1]` returns `true`.

problems.title: Counting Bits
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a nonnegative integer `n`, return the number of set bits for every integer from `0` through `n`.

## Example

Input `5` returns `[0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2]`.

problems.title: Course Schedule
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a course count and directed prerequisite pairs `[course, prerequisite]`, return whether every course can be completed.

## Example

Course count `2` with prerequisites `[[1, 0]]` returns `true`.

problems.title: Decode Ways
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a string of decimal digits, return the number of decodings under the mapping `1` through `26` to letters. A zero cannot be decoded alone and is valid only as part of `10` or `20`.

## Example

Input `"226"` returns `3`.

problems.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Create or initialize a word dictionary that supports adding a word and searching for a pattern. In a search pattern, `.` matches any one character.

## Example

After adding `"bad"` and `"dad"`, searching for `"pad"` returns `false` and searching for `".ad"` returns `true`.

problems.title: Encode and Decode Strings
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Create or initialize a codec that can encode a list of strings as one string and decode that string to recover the original list. Only round-trip behavior is prescribed; any encoding format is valid.

## Example

Create a codec, encode `["lint", "code", "love", "you"]`, then decode the encoded value; the result is the original four-string list.

problems.title: Find Median from Data Stream
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Create or initialize a median tracker that supports adding a number and finding the median of all numbers added so far.

## Example

Create a tracker, add `1`, add `2`, then find the median; the result is `1.5`.

problems.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a rotated sorted integer list, return its minimum value.

## Example

Input `[3, 4, 5, 1, 2]` returns `1`.

problems.title: Graph Valid Tree
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a node count and undirected edges between nodes numbered from zero, return whether they form one tree.

## Example

Node count `5` and edges `[[0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3], [1, 4]]` return `true`.

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given strings, group together strings made from the same character counts. Group and member ordering are unrestricted.

## Example

Input `["eat", "tea", "tan", "ate", "nat", "bat"]` groups as `["bat"]`, `["nat", "tan"]`, and `["ate", "eat", "tea"]`.

problems.title: House Robber
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given values at houses in a line, return the largest sum selectable without choosing adjacent houses.

## Example

Input `[1, 2, 3, 1]` returns `4`.

problems.title: House Robber II
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given values at houses arranged in a circle, return the largest sum selectable without choosing neighboring houses. The first and last houses are adjacent, so they cannot both be selected.

## Example

Input `[2, 3, 2]` returns `3`.

problems.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Create or initialize a trie that supports inserting a word, testing for an exact word, and testing whether any inserted word starts with a prefix.

## Example

After inserting `"apple"`, an exact search for `"apple"` is `true`, an exact search for `"app"` is `false`, and the prefix check for `"app"` is `true`.

problems.title: Insert Interval
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given nonoverlapping intervals sorted by start endpoint and one new interval, insert it and return the merged intervals in ascending position order. Intervals include both endpoints, so intervals that share an endpoint are merged.

## Example

Intervals `[[1, 3], [6, 9]]` with new interval `[2, 5]` return `[[1, 5], [6, 9]]`.

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a binary-tree root, swap left and right children throughout the tree and return the resulting root.

## Example

Tree `[4, 2, 7, 1, 3, 6, 9]` becomes `[4, 7, 2, 9, 6, 3, 1]`.

problems.title: Jump Game
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given maximum jump lengths at successive positions, return whether the final position is reachable from the first.

## Example

Input `[2, 3, 1, 1, 4]` returns `true`.

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a binary-search-tree root and one-based rank `k`, return the value with that rank in ascending value order.

## Example

Tree `[3, 1, 4, null, 2]` with `k = 1` returns `1`.

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a linked-list head, return whether repeatedly following `next` reaches a previously visited node.

## Example

For `[3, 2, 0, -4]` with the tail linked back to the node holding `2`, return `true`.

problems.title: Longest Common Subsequence
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given two strings, return the length of their longest common subsequence; selected characters retain order but need not be adjacent.

## Example

Inputs `"abcde"` and `"ace"` return `3`.

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given integers in arbitrary order, return the length of the longest run of consecutive values.

## Example

Input `[100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2]` returns `4`.

problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given an integer list, return the length of its longest strictly increasing subsequence.

## Example

Input `[10, 9, 2, 5, 3, 7, 101, 18]` returns `4`.

problems.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a string, return a longest contiguous substring that reads the same forward and backward.

## Example

Input `"cbbd"` returns `"bb"`.

problems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a string and replacement budget `k`, return the greatest substring length that can be made one repeated character using at most `k` replacements.

## Example

String `"AABABBA"` with `k = 1` returns `4`.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a string, return the length of its longest contiguous substring containing no repeated character.

## Example

Input `"abcabcbb"` returns `3`.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a binary-search-tree root and two nodes in that tree, return their lowest common ancestor node.

## Example

In tree `[6, 2, 8, 0, 4, 7, 9, null, null, 3, 5]`, nodes `2` and `8` return the root node `6`.

problems.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a binary-tree root, return the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.

## Example

Tree `[3, 9, 20, null, null, 15, 7]` returns `3`.

problems.title: Maximum Product Subarray
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given an integer list, return the largest product of a nonempty contiguous subarray.

## Example

Input `[2, 3, -2, 4]` returns `6`.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given an integer list, return the largest sum of a nonempty contiguous subarray.

## Example

Input `[-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4]` returns `6`.

problems.title: Meeting Rooms
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given meeting intervals `[start, end]`, return whether one attendee can attend all meetings without overlap. A meeting ending when another starts does not overlap it.

## Example

Intervals `[[0, 30], [5, 10], [15, 20]]` return `false`.

problems.title: Meeting Rooms II
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given meeting intervals `[start, end]`, return the minimum number of rooms needed to hold them. A room may be reused when one meeting ends at the next meeting's start.

## Example

Intervals `[[0, 30], [5, 10], [15, 20]]` return `2`.

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given intervals, merge overlaps and return the resulting intervals in ascending position order. Intervals include both endpoints, so intervals that share an endpoint are merged.

## Example

Input `[[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10], [15, 18]]` returns `[[1, 6], [8, 10], [15, 18]]`.

problems.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a list of sorted linked-list heads, merge their values into one sorted linked list and return its head.

## Example

Lists `[1, 4, 5]`, `[1, 3, 4]`, and `[2, 6]` return `[1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6]`.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given two sorted linked-list heads, merge their values into one sorted linked list and return its head.

## Example

Lists `[1, 2, 4]` and `[1, 3, 4]` return `[1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4]`.

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given strings `source` and `target`, return the shortest source substring containing every target character at least as many times as it occurs in the target. Return an empty string if no such substring exists. Inputs are restricted to cases with a unique shortest valid substring.

## Example

Source `"ADOBECODEBANC"` and target `"ABC"` return `"BANC"`.

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given distinct integers drawn from `0` through the list length with one value absent, return the absent value.

## Example

Input `[3, 0, 1]` returns `2`.

problems.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given intervals, return the minimum number that must be removed so the remainder do not overlap. Intervals that only meet at one interval's end and another's start do not overlap.

## Example

Input `[[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4], [1, 3]]` returns `1`.

problems.title: Number of 1 Bits
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a nonnegative integer, return how many bits are set in its binary representation.

## Example

Input `11` returns `3`.

problems.title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a node count and undirected edges between nodes numbered from zero, return the number of connected components.

## Example

Node count `5` with edges `[[0, 1], [1, 2], [3, 4]]` returns `2`.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a rectangular grid of `"1"` land and `"0"` water cells, return the number of land components connected vertically or horizontally.

## Example

Grid `[["1","1","0"], ["1","0","0"], ["0","0","1"]]` returns `2`.

problems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a height grid, return coordinates from which water can reach both the top-or-left boundary and the bottom-or-right boundary by moving to an equal or lower neighbor. Coordinate ordering is unrestricted.

## Example

For heights `[[1,2,2,3,5], [3,2,3,4,4], [2,4,5,3,1], [6,7,1,4,5], [5,1,1,2,4]]`, valid coordinates include `[0,4]`, `[2,2]`, and `[4,0]`.

problems.title: Palindromic Substrings
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a string, return the number of contiguous substrings that read the same forward and backward. Count equal text at different positions separately.

## Example

Input `"aaa"` returns `6`.

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given an integer list, return a list where each position contains the product of every input value except the value at that position.

## Example

Input `[1, 2, 3, 4]` returns `[24, 12, 8, 6]`.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a linked-list head and one-based position `n` from the tail, remove that node and return the resulting head.

## Example

List `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` with `n = 2` returns `[1, 2, 3, 5]`.

problems.title: Reorder List
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a linked-list head, mutate it in place by alternating nodes from the front and back. Return no value.

## Example

List `[1, 2, 3, 4]` is mutated to `[1, 4, 2, 3]`.

problems.title: Reverse Bits
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Interpret the input as a 32-bit bit pattern, reverse its bit positions, and return the resulting 32-bit pattern. The Rust adapter represents both patterns as `i32`; signedness does not change the bits being reversed.

## Example

Input pattern `43261596` returns pattern `964176192`.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a linked-list head, reverse its links and return the new head.

## Example

List `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` returns `[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]`.

problems.title: Rotate Image
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a square matrix, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise in place and return no value.

## Example

Matrix `[[1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7,8,9]]` becomes `[[7,4,1], [8,5,2], [9,6,3]]`.

problems.title: Same Tree
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given two binary-tree roots, return whether both trees have the same shape and equal values at corresponding nodes.

## Example

Trees `[1, 2, 3]` and `[1, 2, 3]` return `true`.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a rotated sorted integer list and a target, return the index where the target occurs. If the target is absent, return the sentinel `-1`.

## Example

List `[4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2]` with target `0` returns `4`.

problems.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Create or initialize a tree codec that can serialize a tree as a string and deserialize that string to reconstruct the tree. Only round-trip tree structure and values are prescribed; any encoding format is valid.

## Example

Create a codec, serialize tree `[1, 2, 3, null, null, 4, 5]`, then deserialize the encoded value; the result is an equivalent tree.

problems.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a matrix, mutate it in place so every row and column containing an input zero becomes all zeroes. Return no value.

## Example

Matrix `[[1,1,1], [1,0,1], [1,1,1]]` becomes `[[1,0,1], [0,0,0], [1,0,1]]`.

problems.title: Spiral Matrix
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a matrix, return its values in clockwise spiral order starting at the top-left corner.

## Example

Input `[[1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7,8,9]]` returns `[1,2,3,6,9,8,7,4,5]`.

problems.title: Subtree of Another Tree
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given roots of two binary trees, return whether the second tree occurs in the first with identical shape and values.

## Example

Tree `[3, 4, 5, 1, 2]` and candidate `[4, 1, 2]` return `true`.

problems.title: Sum of Two Integers
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given two integers, return their sum.

## Example

Inputs `2` and `3` return `5`.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given an integer list and `k`, return `k` values with the greatest occurrence counts in any order. If several values tie at the frequency boundary for the final positions, any selection among those tied values is valid.

## Example

List `[1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3]` with `k = 2` returns values `1` and `2`.

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given an integer list and target, return two distinct valid indices whose values sum to the target. Index ordering is unrestricted.

## Example

List `[2, 7, 11, 15]` with target `9` returns indices `0` and `1`.

problems.title: Unique Paths
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given grid dimensions `rows` and `columns`, return the number of paths from the top-left to bottom-right when each move goes right or down.

## Example

Dimensions `3` by `7` return `28`.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given two strings, return whether they contain exactly the same characters with the same counts.

## Example

Inputs `"anagram"` and `"nagaram"` return `true`.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a string, ignore non-alphanumeric characters and letter case, then return whether the remaining characters form a palindrome.

## Example

Input `"A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"` returns `true`.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a string of bracket characters, return whether every opening bracket is closed by the matching type in properly nested order.

## Example

Input `"()[]{}"` returns `true`.

problems.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a binary-tree root, return whether every node obeys strict binary-search-tree ordering throughout its subtrees.

## Example

Tree `[2, 1, 3]` returns `true`.

problems.title: Word Break
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a string and dictionary of words, return whether the string can be split into a sequence of dictionary entries.

## Example

String `"leetcode"` with dictionary `["leet", "code"]` returns `true`.

problems.title: Word Search
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a character grid and a word, return whether the word can be formed by vertically or horizontally adjacent cells. Each grid cell may be used at most once in one word.

## Example

Grid `[["A", "B", "C", "E"], ["S", "F", "C", "S"], ["A", "D", "E", "E"]]` returns `true` for `"ABCCED"`.

problems.title: Word Search II
problems.statement_markdown:
## Task

Given a character grid and candidate words, return every candidate that can be formed by vertically or horizontally adjacent cells without reusing a cell within one word. Result ordering is unrestricted.

## Example

Grid `[["o", "a", "a", "n"], ["e", "t", "a", "e"], ["i", "h", "k", "r"], ["i", "f", "l", "v"]]` with words `["oath", "pea", "eat", "rain"]` returns `["eat", "oath"]` in either order.
